title: Managing a personal brand: Fast Company's 196-point guide for leaders
tldr: A deep dive into personal brand-building, opening with the Staples Baddie TikTok phenomenon as a case study in unexpected, human-centered creator content that works for brands. Useful reference for executive positioning and employee-generated content.
why_fresh: Fresh framing around employee/creator-led brand building
angle: How employee-generated 'weird' content (the Staples Baddie) beats polished brand campaigns and what governance it needs.

title: Internal communicators need to think like product managers
tldr: Argues internal comms should shift from a publisher mindset (editorial calendars, newsletters) to a product-manager one focused on helping employees understand and act. A genuine reframe for the discipline.
why_fresh: New mental model for internal comms
angle: Why treating internal comms as a product (with users, jobs-to-be-done, and metrics) changes everything about employee engagement.

title: Why we let AI write for us. It's not really about saving time
tldr: Argues we outsource writing to AI out of confidence gaps, not time pressure — flooding channels with 'gray, flavorless mush' that bores audiences. A sharp take on the human premium in content.
why_fresh: Fresh psychological angle on AI writing adoption
angle: The confidence problem behind AI slop — and why human voice is becoming the scarce differentiator.

title: 'Human premium': Why are B2B businesses backing brand?
tldr: Explores why B2B firms are investing in brand and human-led marketing as a premium differentiator in an AI-flooded market. Directly relevant to the people-over-polish thesis.
angle: The rise of the 'human premium' — why B2B is rediscovering brand and personality as AI commoditizes content.

title: When the crisis has no end: Two communicators on the war in Ukraine
tldr: Two Ukrainian comms leaders reflect on doing crisis communications when the crisis has no beginning-stabilization-end arc the textbooks promise. A raw, human take on perpetual crisis comms.
angle: What permanent crisis teaches us: rewriting the crisis-comms playbook when there's no 'after'.

title: 2026 Digital Media Trends: Capturing always-on fandom between releases and seasons
tldr: Deloitte's annual media trends report focuses on how audiences sustain 'always-on' fandom between content drops — a key media-consumption behavior shift for content planners.
why_fresh: New annual data on media-consumption habits
angle: Designing content for 'always-on fandom' — how to keep audiences engaged in the gaps between releases.

title: Omdia: Three in four Americans use smartphones while watching TV
tldr: New data shows 75% of Americans second-screen while watching TV — a hard number on fragmented, multi-device media consumption that reshapes attention strategy.
angle: Designing for the second screen: what 75% dual-screening means for narrative attention and content pacing.

title: How the NFL scaled its global content engine with AI-powered workflows
tldr: Case study on how the NFL built AI-powered content workflows to scale global production. Concrete campaign/ops breakdown Igor can mine for repurposing and modular content lessons.
why_fresh: Vendor case study, but concrete ops detail
angle: Inside the NFL's AI content engine — what modular, AI-assisted workflows look like at global scale.

title: You added Substack to your media list. Now what?
tldr: Practical guide to pitching independent Substack editors as reporters leave institutional newsrooms and take audiences with them. Reflects the ongoing fragmentation of earned media.
why_fresh: Adapts media relations to creator-journalist shift
angle: The independent-journalist media list: how PR must adapt as audiences follow reporters, not outlets.

title: Why beer mats beat billboards when you want to crack a social taboo like debt problems
tldr: Campaign breakdown of 'Say It Over a Drink' — 25 illustrated pub coasters used to get people talking about debt. A clever case study in low-key, human, context-native content.
why_fresh: Novel format/channel for a taboo topic
angle: Small-format, big-taboo: why intimate physical media outperforms billboards for sensitive subjects.

title: Niche Newsletters Turn A Few Thousand Decision Makers Into Premium Ad Inventory
tldr: How tiny-but-targeted newsletters reaching a few thousand decision-makers command premium ad rates — a shift in the economics of owned/niche media.
angle: Small audiences, premium value: why 'a few thousand right people' is the new newsletter growth math.

title: What we've learned from the creator snafus at this year's US Open
tldr: Analysis of creator missteps at the US Open and what they reveal about integrating creators into legacy events. A real-world creator-economy case study with lessons on governance.
angle: When creators meet legacy institutions: governance lessons from the US Open backlash.

title: Mark Ritson on why marketers should stop pretending they know the ROI
tldr: Ritson argues marketers should stop faking precise ROI figures and embrace uncertainty in attribution — a contrarian take on measurement culture.
angle: The honesty gap in content ROI — why fake precision erodes trust with the C-suite.

title: Why 'AI Productivity Gains' Is the Wrong Pitch for Every Stakeholder Above You
tldr: Argues that pitching AI as 'productivity gains' fails with CMOs, CFOs and legal — and shows how to reframe the metric per audience to unlock budget. Useful stakeholder-communication craft.
angle: Reframing AI value per stakeholder — a communication craft lesson for internal buy-in.
